subject: Interim notice: proxy routing disruption affecting dedicated capacity
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Linh Tran <linh.tran@acme-platform.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Interim notice: proxy routing disruption affecting dedicated capacity

Hi Linh and team,

We detected abnormal queuing and elevated latencies impacting requests routed to your dedicated GPU pool (cluster id: redwood-dedicated-usw-42) starting ~08:54 PDT. Initial signals pointed to our proxy-router applying an unexpected routing rule during a traffic surge which, combined with an autoscaler aggregation bug, caused request fanout and queue saturation for a subset of tenants.

What we're doing right now:
- Routing change: we reverted the temporary proxy rule and began draining affected queues to reduce load.
- Autoscaler: we've opened an investigation into why the autoscaler did not evaluate the updated queue depth correctly; mitigation in progress.
- Customer impact: intermittent slow responses and higher error rates for some requests between ~08:54–09:08 PDT. A small percentage of requests saw 5xx errors.

Attachments: incident_log_excerpt.txt (small tail of router logs).

Immediate ask: can you share the best time for a short sync (15–20 min) today so we can walk through the mitigation steps and confirm no lingering impact on your side?

I’ll follow up with a timeline and proposed remediation plan within the hour. Deep apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts production traffic and we’re treating it as a priority.

Thanks,
Grace
Grace O'Connor
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T10:00:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Acme impact — proposed remediation and credit offer

Team,

Recap: Acme Platform observed elevated latencies and some 5xxs during our proxy routing change at ~08:54 PDT. Root signal: proxy-router applied a surge rule that caused cross-tenant fanout; autoscaler aggregation used an incorrect roll-up (bug) that underreported queue depth leading to insufficient scaling. Result: queue saturation on redwood-dedicated-usw-42 for ~14 minutes.

Proposed remediation (to send to customer in next update):
1) Confirmed: revert proxy rule (done).
2) Deploy autoscaler hotfix that corrects aggregation window (POC ready, want a controlled rollout now).
3) Bump fallbacks: temporarily route overflow to burst pool until autoscaler fix is live.
4) Offer: 1 month pro-rated service credit equivalent to 10% of September usage for impacted window + dedicated 1:1 postmortem walk-through.

Attachments for internal review: runbook_patch.diff, metric_dash_snapshot.png.

Can we align on the credit & the messaging? Karthik, can SRE prioritize the autoscaler patch rollout? Ben — legal needs a one-line approval for the credit offer. Marissa — are we good to offer a walkthrough next week (60 min)?

Thanks,
Grace
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Linh Tran <linh.tran@acme-platform.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Update and remediation: proxy routing + autoscaler fixes applied

Hi Linh — quick operational update and next steps.

Root cause summary (preliminary):
- A temporary proxy-router surge rule intended to preferentially route burst traffic misclassified some tenant traffic and duplicated backend fanout under a specific header condition.
- Our autoscaler aggregation job used a 60s roll-up instead of the intended 10s window for that metric, which masked the rapid queue depth increase; the autoscaler therefore did not trigger scale-out quickly enough.

What we implemented (completed):
- Reverted the proxy surge rule at 09:03 PDT and drained impacted queue buckets.
- Deployed autoscaler aggregation hotfix (rolled to 20% of fleet at 12:07 PDT, 100% at 13:12 PDT after verification).
- Adjusted temporary routing policy to send overflow to burst pool with strict tenant isolation.

Impact observed: tail latencies and 5xx spikes subsided by ~09:10 PDT after the revert; autoscaler fix reduced reoccurrence risk for similar rapid surges. Our logs show ~14 minutes of elevated errors for a subset of your requests.

Compensation & next steps: we’d like to offer a pro-rated credit equal to 10% of your September hosted/dedicated spend for the impacted window, plus a 60-minute technical walkthrough of our postmortem and fixes (we’ll share a draft postmortem link). If that works, we’ll record the credit on your account and schedule the walkthrough for next week at your convenience.

Draft postmortem: https://drive.google.com/postmortem-draft?id=abc123
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-ACME-31415

Please let me know if the credit and walkthrough are acceptable and which times next week work for you. We’ll follow with a formal postmortem and the timeline for any longer-term preventive work (routing rule validation and autoscaler metric hardening).

Apologies again for the disruption — we’ll ensure better guardrails are in place so this doesn’t recur.

Best,
Grace
